question: Pick a set of figures from history for your own special dinner party where you get to talk to them.
response:
I would invite Plato, Socrates, René Descartes, and Friedrich Nietzsche to discuss matters related to morality and human knowledge.

Me (the host): "I'm just really curious: Do you think morality is something people are born with—or is it something they pick up along the way? I know at least one of us was totally against ideas like innate knowledge, right?"

Socrates: "Morality must be an innate thing. Otherwise, we wouldn't have been able to discern a whole host of true ideas through the process of dialectic."

René Descartes: "If morality were similar to mathematical truths (which we are certainly born with), I could agree. Unfortunately, there are a lot of conflicting opinions out there that scientifically compel us to refute morality as a naturally occurring instinct."

Friedrich Nietzsche: "The rest of us know this world is irrational at its very core—and yet we continue to act on reason! So I’m with Socrates: morality must come from within."

Plato: "Ditto. Any person who originates from the intelligible realm, prior to their birth, will naturally seek higher truths after arriving in our physical realm."
